column1: # The H200 in numbers: the data behind ideas 9 (the card) and 11 (the funnel). They follow the bars of the core figure
# (figure/beijing_vs_labs.html, fourth edit, Nov 23, 2026). Read by 09_card/build.py and 11_h200_funnel/build.py.
# Tab-separated columns:
#   key      names the lines in each builder's quotes.tsv: <key> (the number's sentence), <key>.date (the page's own date words)
#   dir      toward (blue: ordering, approving, delivering), away (orange: held back), us (grey: Washington's table)
#   tier     open = a press report citing unnamed people; solid = on the record (a government table)
#   card     yes = also on the card; no = on the funnel page only (the card has room for six rows)
#   label    the step, as shown
#   qual     the source's own qualifier before the number ("-" for a sum of the table)
#   number   the number as the source writes it; the builder reads the count from these words and looks for "qual number" in the sentence
#   times    1; each2 = two named buyers, each with this number; table:<sum> = a sum of the project's tables/house_licence_table.tsv,
#            made by a4lib.house() (appr_nv = Nvidia's chips in applications marked "Approved, not shipped"; rwa_nv = Nvidia's in applications marked RWA)
#   by       who reported it, as shown
#   what     a few words on what is counted, as shown
# The rows are separate counts, not one tally. Five are press reports citing unnamed people; two are sums of one United States
# government table of licence applications (status as of May 11, 2026). An application names a data-centre operator or ultimate
# consignee (the table's column; core edit 8b, Nov 25, 2026); it is not an order.
# Dropped in round 4, as in the core: the old multiplied ceiling for Washington's step (our multiplication of a press report: firms times the cap for each).
# Round 5 (Nov 24, 2026): the "by" cell of the two table rows no longer calls the table the Commerce Department's (core edit 6, part 05; not shown on either page).
# Round 11 (Nov 26, 2026, outputs/ROUND11.md thing 2): a press row's label carries the report itself ("Reported: ..."), as the core
# figure's press records now do; the Hong Kong row's second line no longer says in our voice what the chips are (the report's own
# words, "the stockpile of H200 chips", stay quoted under the bar on the funnel page).
# Round 12 (Nov 26, 2026, outputs/ROUND12.md; core batch 14 rows B14-002 to -006): the press rows' labels are level with the
# step cells of the argument's table of numbers ("Reported: under discussion in July 2026", "Reported: delivered by August 2026",
# "Reported: stored in Hong Kong, November 2026"; the first row's label and the words under it make the argument's cell);
# a4lib.funnel() stops if a press row's label is not one of those cells. The Hong Kong row's second line names what is
# counted (the report's "Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence chips"), no longer where they were bound ("to China").
